method: Primary README and source review. No runtime claim for these new candidates.

candidates.classification: Emacs-native SSH broadcast controller over term buffers
features_native: Single-host connection with TRAMP completion
Host selection by regular expression
DSH host files and named @groups, including nested groups
IBuffer marked term buffers become a broadcast group
Controller input is sent to all grouped terminals
Independent Emacs term buffer for each host
limits: No aggregate remote-output buffer: controller contains input and its dummy-shell echo
No per-command completion tracking, exit-status collection, retry policy or finish-based host serialization
Many hosts are tiled as windows automatically
Imports obsolete cl compatibility package; current Emacs runtime not verified here
candidates.default_workflow: After M-x cssh-define-global-bindings: C-= selects host or @group; C-M-= chooses host regexp; in IBuffer C-= controls marked term buffers; type line then RET in controller.
candidates.verdict: Pertinent for interactive parallel input and inventory files; fails aggregate output and true serial jobs.
candidates.evidence_level: Complete primary Lisp source and README reviewed; no SSH runtime test in this subtask.

source_references.finding: Line broadcast without job lifecycle tracking

candidates.classification: Emacs-native menu of named commands on individual TRAMP hosts
features_native: Configure named commands per host
Tabulated command list and RET to run current row
Two completing-read prompts select a host and named command
Synchronous or asynchronous shell-command execution
limits: The Marked column has no corresponding multi-selection execution implementation
Each invocation targets exactly one host and one command
All runs request the same *telecommand-output* buffer; this is reuse, not multi-host aggregation
No inventory-wide parallel/serial runner
Command definitions require Lisp configuration; first-draft snapshot
candidates.default_workflow: Register commands with telecommand-add-command, then M-x telecommand and RET on one row, or M-x telecommand-run and select host/command.
candidates.verdict: Not a multi-server execution solution despite a superficially relevant project description.
candidates.evidence_level: Complete primary Lisp source and README reviewed; no SSH runtime test in this subtask.

source_references.finding: Single host command execution, fixed output buffer
Single host and single command selection
Table rendering; Marked field remains empty

candidates.classification: Emacs-native inventory and individual SSH connection manager
features_native: Persistent host inventory through multisession
Add/edit/delete/select hosts interactively
Import/export inventory and import SSH config
One selected host opens ansi-term
Single-target file copying and SSH key helpers
limits: No multi-host command dispatch
No job concurrency or serial queue
No unified command output view
Does not implement native selected-host batch execution
candidates.default_workflow: M-x add-ssh-machine or M-x import-from-ssh-config; M-x list-ssh-machines; RET connects the host at point.
candidates.verdict: Inventory usability does not satisfy the requested multi-server command execution.
candidates.evidence_level: Complete primary Lisp source and README reviewed; no SSH runtime test in this subtask.

candidates.classification: Emacs-native SSH connection manager and group input sender
features_native: Host discovery from SSH config, known_hosts, encrypted auth-source entries and Docker
Persistent connection history
Live terminal group membership
Send current line, selected region or whole script buffer to every grouped terminal
Separate native Emacs terminal buffers
File upload/download helpers, optional proxy and TOTP paths
limits: Group must be assembled by adding opened terminals; no batch connection of a whole inventory exposed in reviewed source
No unified output buffer
Input broadcast does not await remote command completion or collect command status
No finish-based serialization between hosts
Needs dash/f; advanced authentication paths add sshpass/oathtool setup
candidates.default_workflow: M-x ssh-manager-switch-to-server; C-c C-a in each wanted terminal; M-x ssh-manager for editable command buffer; C-c C-. sends line, C-c C-e sends region, C-c C-c sends buffer. C-c C-r removes current terminal from group.
candidates.verdict: Useful native script-to-group workflow; no scheduler or aggregate result view. No superiority over the shortlisted tools for complete requirements.
candidates.evidence_level: Complete primary Lisp source and README reviewed; no SSH runtime test in this subtask.

source_references.finding: Process input sending; no output merger or job queue

cli_comparison.judgment: For check/script output within ordinary Emacs text, clush is a simpler baseline using OpenSSH. bssh supplies a richer TUI and full session interactions, but neither natively creates one Emacs output buffer per remote host.
